name: audit-docs
description: Adversarial review of the repo's agent-facing instruction files (CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/*, .claude/agents/*) against the actual code, spec, and CLI. Three models, three lenses; arbiter gate; report on pass.

spec.task:
You are one of three adversarial reviewers auditing this repository's AGENT-FACING INSTRUCTION FILES. Your lens: FACTUAL ACCURACY.

The files under audit:
- CLAUDE.md
- .claude/skills/flow-authoring/SKILL.md
- .claude/skills/debug-run/SKILL.md
- .claude/agents/spec-auditor.md
- .claude/agents/run-diagnostician.md

Verify every checkable claim in them against the actual repository: commands and their flags (compare with src/lockstep/cli.py), file paths and module names, exit-code meanings (src/lockstep/__init__.py), verification rule names and severities (src/lockstep/taskgraph.py), interpolation and `when` semantics (src/lockstep/interpolate.py), heal/resume behavior (src/lockstep/roles.py), run-dir layout (SPEC section 10.1 and src/lockstep/store.py, executors/harness.py), and contract names (src/lockstep/contracts.py). A claim that is false, stale, or subtly wrong is a finding; a claim you verified true is not.

Report each problem as a Finding object with EXACTLY these fields: severity (one of "blocker", "major", "minor", "nit"), category (e.g. "doc-inaccuracy"), file (repo-relative path of the INSTRUCTION file containing the bad claim), line (integer or null), claim (one sentence: what the doc says and why it is wrong), evidence (quote the doc AND the code/spec that contradicts it), fix_hint (the corrected statement).

Severity guide: blocker = following the instruction would corrupt state or lose work; major = an agent following it would take a wrong action or run a broken command; minor = misleading but recoverable; nit = imprecise wording.

Your result MUST be ONLY a JSON array of Finding objects — an empty array if all claims check out. You cannot write files; print the JSON array as the final content of your response.

You are one of three adversarial reviewers auditing this repository's AGENT-FACING INSTRUCTION FILES. Your lens: INTERNAL CONSISTENCY.

The files under audit:
- CLAUDE.md
- .claude/skills/flow-authoring/SKILL.md
- .claude/skills/debug-run/SKILL.md
- .claude/agents/spec-auditor.md
- .claude/agents/run-diagnostician.md

Hunt for contradictions: (a) between any two of these files; (b) between these files and the governing documents docs/SPEC.md, docs/AMENDMENTS-r4.md, docs/DEVIATIONS.md (the amendments win over the spec; a logged deviation is sanctioned). Examples of the class: one file calling a rule a warning while another calls it an error; a cadence or process stated differently in two places; a skill contradicting a frozen surface; an agent definition granting tools its own instructions forbid; cross-references to files, skills, or agent names that do not exist.

Report each contradiction as a Finding object with EXACTLY these fields: severity (one of "blocker", "major", "minor", "nit"), category (e.g. "doc-inconsistency"), file (repo-relative path of the instruction file at fault — pick the one that should change), line (integer or null), claim (one sentence naming both sides of the contradiction), evidence (quote BOTH conflicting passages with their file names), fix_hint (which side is right and why).

Your result MUST be ONLY a JSON array of Finding objects — an empty array if the files are consistent. You cannot write files; print the JSON array as the final content of your response.

You are one of three adversarial reviewers auditing this repository's AGENT-FACING INSTRUCTION FILES. Your lens: OPERATIONAL UTILITY — would an agent actually following these instructions succeed?

The files under audit:
- CLAUDE.md
- .claude/skills/flow-authoring/SKILL.md
- .claude/skills/debug-run/SKILL.md
- .claude/agents/spec-auditor.md
- .claude/agents/run-diagnostician.md

Simulate following them. Hunt for: instructions that omit a step the code makes mandatory (check src/lockstep/cli.py and src/lockstep/taskgraph.py for what actually happens); guidance that is dangerous when followed literally (e.g. a recovery command that loses work); critical failure modes the debug playbook does not cover but the code can produce; skill frontmatter descriptions that would fire the skill at the wrong time; agent tool grants that are too broad or too narrow for their stated procedure. Do NOT report topics the files deliberately delegate to docs/SPEC.md — these are working aids, not the spec.

Report each problem as a Finding object with EXACTLY these fields: severity (one of "blocker", "major", "minor", "nit"), category (e.g. "doc-utility"), file (repo-relative instruction file), line (integer or null), claim (one sentence: what an agent would do wrong), evidence (quote the instruction and cite the code behavior that defeats it), fix_hint (string).

Your result MUST be ONLY a JSON array of Finding objects — an empty array if the instructions are operationally sound. You cannot write files; print the JSON array as the final content of your response.
